title: Past Perfect with hadde
goal: Use hadde plus a past participle to show what was already completed before another past point.

objectives.statement: Use hadde plus a past participle to show what was already completed before another past point.

spans.value: Mari is meeting Jonas and Amina at a café after work. Her bus is delayed, and she arrives much later than planned.
Beklager at jeg er så sen!
Det går bra. Vi hadde allerede bestilt da du sendte meldingen.

blocks.translation: It’s fine. We had already ordered when you sent the message.

spans.value: Og servitøren hadde satt maten på bordet før du kom.

blocks.translation: And the waiter had put the food on the table before you arrived.

spans.value: Å nei. Hadde dere begynt på middagen?

blocks.translation: Oh no. Had you started the meal?

spans.value: Nei, vi ventet på deg. Men Amina hadde spist alt brødet.

blocks.translation: No, we waited for you. But Amina had eaten all the bread.

spans.value: Jeg var sulten! Jeg hadde ikke spist siden frokost.

blocks.translation: I was hungry! I hadn’t eaten since breakfast.

spans.value: Jeg forstår. Jeg hadde også glemt matpakken hjemme.

blocks.translation: I understand. I had also forgotten my packed lunch at home.

spans.value: The conversation is about several past events. Mari sent a message. She arrived at the café. Jonas and Amina ordered. The waiter put the food on the table. Amina ate the bread.
Some of these events happened earlier than other past events. Jonas does not simply say that they ordered. He places the ordering before Mari’s message:

no.value: Vi hadde allerede bestilt da du sendte meldingen.

en.value: We had already ordered when you sent the message.

spans.value: This is the central purpose of the
past perfect (pluskvamperfektum)
: it shows that something was already completed before another past point.

sections.title: Looking back from a past point

spans.value: The past perfect consists of:
hadde + past participle
You already know the past participle from the present perfect. The participle does not change here; only the form of ha changes.

no.value: Jeg har spist.

en.value: I have eaten.

no.value: Jeg hadde spist før møtet begynte.

en.value: I had eaten before the meeting began.

spans.value: In the first sentence, har spist connects the completed action to the present. In the second, hadde spist looks back from a point in the past: the beginning of the meeting. Eating was already complete at that point.
Common combinations include:

no.value: hadde spist

en.value: had eaten

no.value: hadde gått

en.value: had gone

no.value: hadde sett

en.value: had seen

no.value: hadde gjort

en.value: had done

no.value: hadde kjøpt

en.value: had bought

no.value: hadde glemt

en.value: had forgotten

no.value: hadde bestilt

en.value: had ordered

no.value: hadde kommet

en.value: had arrived

spans.value: The compact rule is:

statement.value: Use hadde plus a past participle when you need to mark an action as completed before another past event or past situation.

spans.value: Compare these two sentences:

no.value: Da Mari kom, bestilte vi mat.

en.value: When Mari arrived, we ordered food.

no.value: Da Mari kom, hadde vi bestilt mat.

en.value: When Mari arrived, we had ordered food.

spans.value: In the first sentence, Mari arrived and then the group ordered. The simple past, or
past tense (preteritum)
, presents the ordering as part of the main sequence of events.
In the second sentence, the ordering happened before Mari arrived. The past perfect sends the listener one step further back.
A simple timeline makes the difference clear:
Earlier:
The group ordered.
Later past point:
Mari arrived.

no.value: Vi hadde bestilt mat før Mari kom.

en.value: We had ordered food before Mari arrived.

spans.value: The order can also be expressed with the later event first:

no.value: Da Mari kom, hadde vi bestilt mat.

en.value: When Mari arrived, we had ordered food.

spans.value: The position of the clauses does not decide which action happened first. The form hadde bestilt marks the earlier completed action.
Here are further contrasts:

no.value: Da filmen begynte, fant vi plassene våre.

en.value: When the film began, we found our seats.

no.value: Da filmen begynte, hadde vi funnet plassene våre.

en.value: When the film began, we had found our seats.

spans.value: In the first sentence, finding the seats belongs to the sequence beginning when the film started. In the second, the seats were found before the film started.

no.value: Da læreren kom, åpnet elevene bøkene.

en.value: When the teacher arrived, the pupils opened their books.

no.value: Da læreren kom, hadde elevene åpnet bøkene.

en.value: When the teacher arrived, the pupils had opened their books.

spans.value: Again, the second version places the opening of the books before the teacher’s arrival.
The auxiliary hadde stays the same with every subject:

no.value: Jeg hadde spist.

en.value: I had eaten.

no.value: Du hadde spist.

en.value: You had eaten.

no.value: Hun hadde spist.

en.value: She had eaten.

no.value: Vi hadde spist.

en.value: We had eaten.

no.value: De hadde spist.

en.value: They had eaten.

spans.value: This makes the structure relatively economical. Once you have chosen the correct past participle, you do not need to change hadde for person or number.
The participle is the same one used after har:

no.value: Han har gått hjem.

en.value: He has gone home.

no.value: Han hadde gått hjem før jeg ringte.

en.value: He had gone home before I called.

no.value: De har sett filmen.

en.value: They have seen the film.

no.value: De hadde sett filmen før.

en.value: They had seen the film before.

spans.value: A common mistake is to put a past-tense verb after hadde:

no.value: Han hadde gikk hjem.

en.value: He had went home.

spans.value: This is not correct. After hadde, use the past participle:

no.value: Han hadde gått hjem.

en.value: He had gone home.

spans.value: Similarly:

no.value: Vi hadde så filmen.

en.value: We had saw the film.

spans.value: The correct form is:

no.value: Vi hadde sett filmen.

en.value: We had seen the film.

spans.value: Do not create a new participle rule for the past perfect. Reuse the participles you know from the present perfect: har gått becomes hadde gått, har sett becomes hadde sett, and har gjort becomes hadde gjort.
Words such as allerede and før often make the timeline especially clear.

no.value: Toget hadde allerede gått da vi kom til stasjonen.

en.value: The train had already left when we arrived at the station.

no.value: Nora hadde låst døren før hun gikk til bussen.

en.value: Nora had locked the door before she went to the bus.

no.value: Jeg hadde lest rapporten før møtet startet.

en.value: I had read the report before the meeting started.

no.value: De hadde ryddet kjøkkenet da gjestene kom.

en.value: They had cleaned the kitchen when the guests arrived.

spans.value: The past point may be an event, as in da gjestene kom, or a past situation:

no.value: Erik var trøtt fordi han hadde sovet dårlig.

en.value: Erik was tired because he had slept badly.

spans.value: Erik’s tiredness is in the past. His poor sleep happened earlier and explains that past situation.

no.value: Leiligheten var tom. De forrige eierne hadde flyttet ut.

en.value: The flat was empty. The previous owners had moved out.

spans.value: The second sentence looks further back and explains why the flat was empty.
Sometimes the later past point is clear from the surrounding story and does not need to appear in the same sentence:

no.value: Jeg kom til kontoret klokka ni. Alle de andre hadde begynt å jobbe.

en.value: I arrived at the office at nine. Everyone else had started working.

spans.value: The arrival at the office provides the reference point. The others started working before that arrival.

sections.title: Returning to Mari, Jonas, and Amina

spans.value: After dinner, Mari explains why she was late.
Jeg gikk til feil bussholdeplass fordi jeg fulgte den gamle bussruta til kafeen.

blocks.translation: I went to the wrong bus stop because I followed the old bus route to the café.

spans.value: Men hadde du ikke sjekket den nye bussruta til kafeen?

blocks.translation: But hadn’t you checked the new bus route to the café?

spans.value: Jo, men jeg hadde lagret den gamle ruta på telefonen.

blocks.translation: Yes, but I had saved the old route on my phone.

spans.value: Da du oppdaget feilen, hadde bussen på den nye ruta gått?

blocks.translation: When you discovered the mistake, had the bus on the new route left?

spans.value: Ja. Den hadde akkurat kjørt fra riktig holdeplass. Derfor måtte jeg vente på den neste.

blocks.translation: Yes. It had just left the correct stop. That’s why I had to wait for the next one.

spans.value: The main past sequence is that Mari followed the old route to the wrong stop, discovered the mistake, and waited for another bus. The past perfect supplies earlier background:

items.value: She had checked the new bus route to the café.
She had saved the old route on her phone before the trip.
The bus on the new route had left the correct stop before she could take it.

spans.value: This is useful in storytelling because it separates the main sequence from earlier completed events. It lets the listener understand why a past situation developed as it did.
Compare:

no.value: Mari oppdaget feilen, og bussen gikk.

en.value: Mari discovered the mistake, and the bus left.

spans.value: This presents two events in the main sequence.

no.value: Da Mari oppdaget feilen, hadde bussen gått.

en.value: When Mari discovered the mistake, the bus had left.

spans.value: This says the bus was already gone when she discovered the error.

sections.title: A likely misconception: not every earlier event needs hadde

spans.value: The past perfect is most useful when you are looking back from an established past point and need to make the relationship clear. It does not have to replace every past-tense verb in a chronological story.

no.value: Jeg sto opp, spiste frokost og gikk til jobben.

en.value: I got up, ate breakfast, and went to work.

spans.value: The sequence is already presented in order. Simple past is natural throughout.
Now imagine that the story begins at work:

no.value: Da jeg kom på jobben, hadde jeg allerede spist frokost.

en.value: When I arrived at work, I had already eaten breakfast.

spans.value: The arrival is the later past point. The breakfast is earlier background, so hadde spist is useful.
Another common problem is reversing the forms. Suppose the stated order is: first the film began, and then we arrived at the cinema.

no.value: Da vi hadde kommet til kinoen, begynte filmen.

en.value: When we had arrived at the cinema, the film began.

spans.value: This incorrectly places the past perfect on the later arrival. The film’s beginning is the earlier completed event:

no.value: Da vi kom til kinoen, hadde filmen begynt.

en.value: When we arrived at the cinema, the film had begun.

spans.value: Ask yourself one practical question:

statement.value: At that later moment in the past, what had already happened?

spans.value: The answer to that question is the event that normally takes hadde plus a past participle.

sections.title: Transfer: arriving at a holiday cabin

spans.value: Now move to a different situation. Henrik and Lea reached a rented cabin late on Friday evening. Their friends had arrived earlier and prepared several things before Henrik and Lea got there.
Relevant facts might include lighting the fire, buying food, making the beds, and finding the key. The later past point is Henrik and Lea’s arrival.
Useful models are:

no.value: Da Henrik og Lea kom fram, hadde vennene tent opp i peisen.

en.value: When Henrik and Lea arrived, their friends had lit the fire.

no.value: De hadde kjøpt mat før Henrik og Lea kom fram.

en.value: They had bought food before Henrik and Lea arrived.

no.value: Vennene hadde redd opp sengene før Henrik og Lea kom fram.

en.value: The friends had made the beds before Henrik and Lea arrived.

no.value: De hadde gjort sengene klare før gjestene kom.

en.value: They had prepared the beds before the guests arrived.

prompt.value: In the café scene, read these two statements: «Da Mari kom, hadde vi bestilt mat.» «Da Mari kom, hadde servitøren satt maten på bordet.» Choose the complete interpretation of both timelines.

options.text: I begge setningene kom Mari først; vi bestilte mat og servitøren satte maten på bordet etterpå.
options.why: This reverses the earlier and later events marked by the past perfect.

options.text: I setningen «Da Mari kom, hadde vi bestilt mat» viser «hadde bestilt» at vi bestilte mat før Mari kom. I setningen «Da Mari kom, hadde servitøren satt maten på bordet» viser «hadde satt» at servitøren satte maten på bordet før Mari kom.
options.why: Both hadde phrases mark actions completed before Mari’s arrival.

stem.value: Which option identifies the action completed first and Mari’s later arrival in both statements?

prompt.value: We cleaned the kitchen before the guests arrived. Build the Norwegian sentence with the later event first.

explanation.value: Hadde + past participle places one completed event before another past reference point.

prompt.value: Choose the correct past participle after hadde. The context is guests arriving after breakfast.

spans.value: Da gjestene kom, hadde vi allerede
frokost.

prompt.value: Complete the second sentence with the past participle of bestille. The first sentence supplies the past reference point; no før phrase is provided.

spans.value: Møtet startet klokka ni. Vi hadde allerede
mat.

prompt.value: Write a short guided account in Norwegian about Mari’s delay. State that she went to the wrong bus stop because she followed the old bus route to the café, discovered the mistake, and waited for the next bus. Also include these earlier facts: she checked the new bus route, she saved the old route on her phone, and the bus on the new route left the correct stop. Keep the main events in the simple past and mark each earlier completed fact with hadde plus a past participle. Write 4–6 sentences.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the Norwegian account against the task and report concrete evidence for each criterion. Do not award a criterion without explicit language evidence.

criteria.instruction: States that Mari followed the old bus route to the wrong stop, discovered the mistake, and waited for the next bus in simple past.
Uses hadde followed by an accurate past participle for each supplied earlier fact: checking the new route, saving the old route, and the bus leaving the correct stop.

prompt.value: The guests arrived first, and only afterward did we clean the kitchen. Select the one token that is wrong/needs changing in this timeline.

payload.feedback: Remove the second «hadde». The arrival is earlier, so keep «hadde kommet» and use simple past for later cleaning: «Da gjestene hadde kommet, ryddet vi kjøkkenet.»

prompt.value: Write four short affirmative Norwegian statements about the holiday cabin. Henrik and Lea arrived late on Friday evening. Before they arrived, their friends lit the fire, bought food, made the beds, and found the key. Show each completed preparation with hadde plus a past participle.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the Norwegian statements against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept natural Bokmål variants for the supplied facts.

criteria.instruction: Writes four affirmative Norwegian statements covering lighting the fire, buying food, making the beds, and finding the key.
Uses hadde followed by an accurate past participle for each preparation.
Places each preparation clearly before Henrik and Lea arrived.

prompt.value: At a railway station, Sara arrived late. Write exactly two Norwegian sentences stating two natural things that had already happened before she arrived. Choose your own actions rather than copying a complete lesson sentence. Use hadde plus a past participle in each sentence.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept natural Bokmål variants that fit the station context, but not a complete sentence copied verbatim from the lesson.

criteria.instruction: Writes exactly two Norwegian sentences with two distinct completed actions before Sara arrived.
Uses hadde followed by an accurate past participle in each sentence.
Makes both actions clearly earlier than Sara’s arrival.
